one who knows. חֲכַם הרזים He who knows the secrets (minds of men).
units: <cite ref="Berakhot 58a:3">Ber. 58ᵃ</cite>; Tosef. ib. VII (VI), 2; <cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 21:2">Num. R. s. 21</cite>, beg.

senses.gloss: wise man, scholar; esp. Ḥakham, a scholar’s title, less than Rabbi.
units: <cite ref="Pirkei Avot 4:1">Ab. IV, 1</cite> <he>איזהו ח׳</he> who is a wise man? <cite ref="Sanhedrin 21a:20">Snh. 21ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="II Samuel 13:3">II Sam. XIII, 3</cite>) <he>איש ח׳ לרשעה</he> a man wise for wickedness (artful).
<cite ref="Gittin 67a:8">Gitt. 67ᵃ</cite> <he>ח׳ וסופר</he> is a scholar and a scribe; <he>ח׳ לכשירצה</he> might be a scholar, if he wanted.
Hor. 13ᵇ ר״מ ח׳ R. M. was the Ḥakham (counselor); a. v. fr.—Pl. חֲכָמִים, frequ. in the sense of a number of scholars, as opposed to a single authority.
<cite ref="Chullin 85a:9">Ḥull. 85ᵃ</cite> <he>ראה רבי</he> … <he>ושנאו בלשון ח׳</he> Rabbi approving of R. Meir’s opinion …, recorded it in the Mishnah as the opinion of ‘scholars’.
<cite ref="Mishnah Berakhot 1:1">Ber. I, 1</cite>; a. v. fr.—<he>חַכְמֵי אומות העולם</he> gentile scholars (philosophers), <he>חכמי ישראל</he> Jewish scholars.
Pes. 94ᵇ; a. fr.—תַּלְמִיד חָכָם (= תלמיד וח׳, cmp. חָבֵר, abbr. ת״ח) title of a student, disciple, scholar.
<cite ref="Chagigah 15b:10">Ḥag. 15ᵇ</cite> <he>ת״ח אע״פ שסרח וכ׳</he> a scholar’s learning is not to be despised, even if he has gone astray.
Ḥull. 9ᵃ ת״ח צריך וכ׳ in order to be recognised as a Talmid Ḥakham, one must have learned three things &c.; a. v. fr.—Pl. תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים.
<cite ref="Berakhot 64a:8">Ber. 64ᵃ</cite> <he>ת״ה מרבים וכ׳</he> scholars increase the peace of the world; a. v. fr.
